This is not a live account screenshot.
svg.text: Bot configuration, purchase and withdrawal schedule, and period analysis with activity history and Parqet CSV export

Choose a custom date range or an interval between withdrawals to review activity and prepare a Parqet export.
Current value of BTC bought in this period minus trading fees
Kraken saved withdrawal method: Example Bitcoin wallet (fictional)
Manual withdrawals are available. Automatic withdrawals may remain disabled.
The button withdraws the entire available BTC balance, less the exchange withdrawal fee. LIVE_TRADING must be enabled; automatic withdrawals may remain disabled and their threshold does not apply.
Configure KRAKEN_WITHDRAW_KEY in .env for Kraken, or WITHDRAW_ADDRESS and WITHDRAW_NETWORK for Bitvavo. Kraken resolves the saved method to its destination address. A confirmation is
required before submission. Submitted manual withdrawals appear in Activity immediately and count toward Parqet exports only after confirmation. Failed or unverified withdrawals are excluded.

Purchase shows the current BTC price, available fiat balance, next purchase and countdown. The current BTC price is fetched from Kraken’s public BTC-to-fiat pages when the report loads and is shown in
the selected display currency. The purchase interval is the time from the last purchase to the next deposit day divided by the estimated number of purchases the current balance can cover, including

estimated fees and the planning buffer. Without a previous purchase, the current time is used. The next purchase is the last purchase time plus this interval; elapsed time reduces the remaining wait. Bot
checks update the schedule; open or unconfirmed orders block further purchases.
Withdrawal shows the available BTC balance on the selected exchange and an estimated automatic withdrawal date and countdown. The threshold uses the exchange BTC balance valued in the purchase

currency, including BTC acquired outside the bot. Expected monthly deposit is a forecast assumption saved in this browser: future deposits are added on the configured deposit day and purchase intervals

are recalculated for each calendar month. The forecast assumes the current BTC price, order size and estimated costs; it does not initiate deposits or change trading. The BTC still needed is the withdrawal

threshold divided by the current BTC price in the purchase currency, minus the available exchange BTC balance. Dividing this shortfall by the estimated BTC amount per purchase and rounding up gives the

remaining number of purchases. Starting with the next scheduled purchase, the forecast projects these purchases using the current budget and interval; when further funds are needed, it adds the expected

monthly deposit on each configured deposit day, carries over unused funds and recalculates the interval using the actual calendar month and estimated order costs including fees and the planning buffer.

The estimated withdrawal date is when the final required purchase is projected to occur; the actual withdrawal is submitted during a subsequent eligible bot check. If the threshold is already reached, the
estimate is the current time. The remaining time is the estimated withdrawal date and time minus the current time, updated every second and never shown as negative. Actual prices, deposits, fees and
execution can change the result. Automatic withdrawals must be enabled for an estimate. Balance timestamps show the last account check; the countdowns update every second.
Period analysis, Parqet export and local activity history.

These notes apply to the date filters in Period analysis, the Activity table and the Download Parqet CSV button. Historical fiat amounts are grouped by their original currency and converted separately to the
selected display currency. Parqet CSV exports use EUR. Choose an interval between bot-recorded BTC withdrawals or set a custom date range. The Parqet CSV uses the complete interval after the previous

confirmed withdrawal through the last confirmed withdrawal in the selected date range. It combines real purchase costs and trading fees in EUR with the ending withdrawal’s net BTC after network fees; later
purchases are excluded. The selected range must contain a confirmed withdrawal whose complete interval includes a real purchase. Dry-run purchases are shown separately and excluded from the CSV.
Delete removes a purchase from local history only; it cannot reverse an exchange order.
The default Docker Compose configuration publishes the dashboard port on all host interfaces. Other devices can connect using the Docker host’s IP address where allowed by the firewall. HTTP does not
encrypt sign-in credentials; use HTTPS through a reverse proxy on untrusted networks.
